title: Auto-curate priority playbooks and incident concierge
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: On-call engineers frequently spend the first 10-15 minutes of an incident assembling context: which runbook applies, where the recent traces live, which dashboards to open, and who to loop in. This delays mitigation and increases blast radius for flapping services.

Goal: Build an "incident concierge" feature that auto-curates a ranked list of playbooks for a triggered alert, creates a Slack incident thread pre-populated with the top playbook steps, attaches the top 3 related traces and a short metrics snapshot, and schedules a postmortem skeleton if severity >= P1. Concierge should integrate with PagerDuty signals to respect escalation policies and on-call profiles.

Scope: Mend the end-to-end flow from alert -> curated playbook suggestions -> Slack thread starter -> optional postmortem skeleton creation. Leverage existing tracing hooks and metric summaries from the telemetry pipeline. This ticket implements the core backend orchestration, mapping heuristics, and a Slack starter payload. UI polish and full console integration will be follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: When a PagerDuty alert arrives, the concierge returns a ranked list of candidate runbooks (score and rationale) within 4s
Slack incident starter posts a thread to the service channel with: summary, 3 suggested next steps, links to top 3 traces, and metrics snapshot
If alert severity >= P1 and policy allows, a postmortem skeleton (title + template) is created in the configured postmortem folder and a link is added to the Slack thread
On-call routing respects PagerDuty schedule and does not create duplicate pages for the same alert group within 10m
End-to-end smoke test: simulated SLO breach alert results in concierge flow wired to a test Slack workspace and creates a postmortem stub
technical_notes: Mapping heuristic: combine alert fingerprint, service tags, recently-running traces (last 30m), and historical incident-match model to score playbooks
Privacy: traces must be redacted using existing telemetry PII filters before embedding links/snippets
Failure modes: if trace API timeouts, still post playbook suggestions derived from alert metadata and metrics snapshot
Rate limits: Slack starter payloads will be throttled to 1 per service per 5 minutes; PagerDuty deduplication used upstream
Data retention: postmortem skeletons are simple references and metadata only; we do not replicate raw traces into postmortem storage
progress_updates: 2025-03-03: Spike complete - validated we can fetch a top-3 trace list within 700ms for high-cardinality services using the trace index

2025-03-06: Prototype of playbook scorer implemented (logistic regression over features: alert fingerprint match, tag overlap, recent trace similarity). Achieves 78% precision on historical incident set
2025-03-09: Slack starter payload schema reviewed with Design. Decided to use a minimal thread-first approach (title + three bullets + links) rather than modal to avoid blocking responders
2025-03-12: PagerDuty integration stubbed; using PD webhook attributes to determine severity and on-call schedule. Ran canary tests against test-schedules
2025-03-15: Security sign-off checkpoint: redaction pipeline integration added for traces; discovered an edge case with HTTP headers that needs a follow-up (ENG-48301)
2025-03-18: Backend orchestration endpoint /concierge/v1/incident prepared; end-to-end smoke runs green in staging except for flaky dashboard snapshot generator (investigating)
review_feedback: PM (Lina Morales): Emphasize minimizing noisy suggestions; prefer 'no suggestion' over wrong suggestion. Add confidence score to payload
Design (Marco Liu): Slack thread should include an 'I want this to be primary' button to let the responder claim the playbook and trigger a faster runbook lock
Security (Priya Nair): Ensure we never expose user tokens in starter payloads. Prefer links that require auth rather than full text dumps of trace spans
Observability Lead (Jon Park): Move initial scoring into nearline service to reduce tail latency; heavy ML scoring can be async with fallback simple rules
